newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK, Taiwan may have shipping deal in April - paper.
newsitem.headline: HK, Taiwan may have shipping deal in April - paper.

text.p: Hong Kong and Taiwan may reach agreement before the end of April on shipping arrangements after the British colony reverts to Chinese rule on July 1, the South China Morning Post reported on Saturday.

Despite the absence of an official Taiwan negotiator, a speedy wrap-up of the deal was possible because Beijing and Taipei had adopted a flexible stance, the paper quoted unidentified sources as saying.

Beijing has appointed Hong Kong Shipowners' Association (HKSOA) chairman George Chao to negotiate on its behalf, but has refused to accept Taipei's National Association of Chinese Shipowners, because the name implies that there are two Chinas.
As a result, discussions had stalled pending Taipei's approval of the Taiwan Cross Strait Shipping Association (TCSSA) as its official negotiating body, the newspaper said.
Beijing has regarded Taiwan as a renegade province ever since a civil war separated the two in 1949 and fiercely opposes any moves that run against its "one China" policy.
Hong Kong will become a Special Administrative Region under China on July 1 after more than 150 years of British colonial rule.

The HKSOA proposed Hong Kong-registered ships fly the Special Administrative Region (SAR) flag when entering Taiwan waters. Taiwan ships should hoist their "plum blossom" flag, which is Taiwan's emblem, instead of the flag of Taiwan's government while in Hong Kong waters, it added.

Taipei proposes that Hong Kong ships lower all flags while in Taiwanese waters and that Taiwan's ships do the same in Hong Kong waters. Hong Kong's post-handover constitution states that after July 1 Hong Kong-registered ships on international routes must fly China's national flag along with the SAR flag.
